summary: Emilie Li (SCAD) and Sumit Saurabh (Design Circle International) covered creative-career pathways for TOC counselors. Li cited SCAD's own research that 85% of career success comes from soft skills versus 15% from technical execution, noted that 63% of SCAD's degree programs are STEM-designated (unlocking 3 years of OPT), and described SCADpro, SCAD's in-house studio that pairs student teams with Fortune 500 companies. Saurabh then contrasted portfolio expectations across geographies: the USA rewards polished final execution, the UK/Europe rewards visible process and sketchbooks, and Indian government design colleges (NIFT/NID/UCEED) are driven almost entirely by entrance-exam scores rather than portfolios.
keyInsights: SCAD's own stat: 85% of career success comes from soft skills, 15% from technical skill.
63% of SCAD degree programs are STEM-designated, giving international grads 3 years of OPT.
SCADpro pairs student teams with Fortune 500 companies (Google, BMW, NASA, Coca-Cola) on real projects.
Portfolio expectations diverge sharply by geography: USA (polished execution) vs UK/Europe (process/sketchbooks) vs Indian govt colleges (pure entrance-exam driven).
